problem_text: Let A be the ring k[[x_1, ..., x_n]], where k is a field, n in N, n != 0. Show that there is no isomorphism A ⊗_k A ≅ k[[x_1, ..., x_n, y_1, ..., y_n]].
solution_text: Proof: Consider the element 1 + x_1*y_1. In k[[x_1,...,x_n, y_1,...,y_n]], this is a unit with inverse Σ_{i=0}^∞ (-x_1*y_1)^i = Σ_{i=0}^∞ (-1)^i x_1^i y_1^i (geometric series converges in the m-adic topology). We show 1 + x_1*y_1 is NOT a unit in A ⊗_k A. Suppose it were, with inverse u = Σ_{j=1}^m f_j(x) g_j(y) (finite sum, since elements of the tensor product are finite sums of products). Via the natural injection A⊗_k A → k[[x,y]], we get Σ_{j=1}^m f_j(x) g_j(y) = Σ_{i=0}^∞ (-1)^i x_1^i y_1^i in k[[x,y]]. Comparing coefficients of x_1^a y_1^b: the coefficient matrix M_{ab} = Σ_j [x_1^a]f_j · [y_1^b]g_j equals (-1)^a δ_{ab}. This is an infinite diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries, hence has infinite rank. But M = Σ_j v_j w_j^T where v_j = ([x_1^a]f_j)_a and w_j = ([y_1^b]g_j)_b, so rank(M) ≤ m < ∞. Contradiction. Therefore 1 + x_1*y_1 is not a unit in A ⊗_k A. Since being a unit is preserved under ring isomorphism, no isomorphism A ⊗_k A ≅ k[[x_1,...,x_n, y_1,...,y_n]] exists.
solution_summary: 1+x_1*y_1 is a unit in k[[x,y]] (geometric series converges) but not in A⊗_k A (inverse is a non-separable power series, proven by rank argument: infinite diagonal matrix has infinite rank but finite sum of outer products has bounded rank). Unit status is isomorphism-invariant, so no isomorphism exists.
answer: There is no k-algebra isomorphism A ⊗_k A ≅ k[[x_1,...,x_n, y_1,...,y_n]] because 1+x_1*y_1 is a unit in the latter (geometric series converges in the complete ring) but not in the former (the inverse Σ(-1)^i x_1^i y_1^i is a non-separable power series not in the tensor product, proven by the rank argument).
structure_features: Non-isomorphism proof via ring-theoretic invariant (unit property); key structural difference between algebraic tensor product (finite sums of separable terms) and completed tensor product (all power series); rank argument as the engine for proving non-separability
key_objects: k[[x_1,...,x_n, y_1,...,y_n]] multivariable power series ring
key_insight: 1+x_1*y_1 is a unit in the complete ring k[[x,y]] (geometric series converges) but not in the non-complete algebraic tensor product A⊗_k A (inverse is a non-separable power series; rank argument proves it is not a finite sum of products)
expected_ai_method: Bare AI would try to compare standard ring invariants (Krull dimension, Noetherianness, embedding dimension) which all match, or attempt to construct/disprove an explicit isomorphism by mapping generators, without recognizing that the key invariant is the unit structure (completeness)
correct_method: Test whether 1+x_1*y_1 is a unit in each ring: it is in the complete ring (geometric series) but not in the tensor product (rank argument proves the inverse is non-separable). Unit property is isomorphism-invariant.

rounds.question: 描述这道题的结构：两个环分别是什么？我们需要证明什么？
rounds.expected_answer: A = k[[x_1,...,x_n]]，需证 A⊗_k A 与 k[[x_1,...,x_n, y_1,...,y_n]] 不同构。这是一个交换代数中的非同构证明问题，n≥1。

rounds.question: 列出所有可能区分这两个环的环论不变量
rounds.expected_answer: Krull维数、Noether性、完备性、单位群结构、极大理想生成元数、剩余域、嵌入维数……

rounds.question: 试着比较Krull维数和嵌入维数
rounds.expected_answer: 两环的Krull维数都是2n，嵌入维数都是2n，极大理想都由2n个元素生成。这些标准不变量无法区分它们。

rounds.question: 思考A⊗_k A中的元素与k[[x,y]]中的元素有什么结构差异？张量积中的元素长什么样？
rounds.expected_answer: A⊗_k A的元素是有限个乘积f(x)g(y)之和——'可分'幂级数。k[[x,y]]包含任意幂级数，包括不可分的如Σx_1^i y_1^i。

rounds.question: 考虑元素1+x_1*y_1。它在每个环中是否是单位？为什么？
rounds.expected_answer: 在k[[x,y]]中是单位：(1+x_1*y_1)^{-1}=Σ(-x_1*y_1)^i（几何级数在m-adic拓扑中收敛）。在A⊗_k A中，逆元需要是Σ(-1)^i x_1^i y_1^i，这是无穷个可分项之和，不是有限和，可能不在张量积中。

rounds.question: 严格证明Σ(-1)^i x_1^i y_1^i不能写成有限个乘积f_j(x)g_j(y)之和
rounds.expected_answer: 若Σ(-1)^i x_1^i y_1^i = Σ_{j=1}^m f_j(x)g_j(y)，则系数矩阵M_{ab}=Σ_j [x_1^a]f_j·[y_1^b]g_j = (-1)^a δ_{ab}。这是无穷对角矩阵（非零对角元），有无穷秩。但M=Σ_j v_j w_j^T是有限个外积之和，秩≤m。矛盾！

rounds.question: 把以上步骤组合起来，完成证明
rounds.expected_answer: 1+x_1*y_1在k[[x,y]]中是单位但在A⊗_k A中不是单位。单位性在环同构下保持，故两环不同构。QED。

analysis_metadata.notes: FATE-X problem 67: Commutative algebra / dimension theory. Key proof technique: unit property as isomorphism invariant, rank argument for non-separability. The Lean proof is 'sorry' (no formal proof provided), so the mathematical proof was constructed from scratch. The proof is clean and elegant: 1+x_1*y_1 is a unit in the complete ring but not in the algebraic tensor product, proven by the rank argument (infinite diagonal matrix has infinite rank vs. finite sum of outer products has bounded rank).
